profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21721 Filigree Court, Suite A, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC6 data center at 21721 Filigree Court, Suite A, in Ashburn, Virginia, one node in Equinix's cluster of buildings spread across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC6 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 59,374 square feet of space, N+1 redundancy for both its UPS and generator systems, and nine compliance standards including HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and LEED certification. LEED certification is a fact Equinix confirms for DC6 that does not appear on the DC4 or DC16 pages nearby on this same campus, though Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC6 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and Equinix markets DC1 through DC6 and DC10 through DC12 collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the East Coast, without singling out DC6's own peering density or customer roster.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
Equinix DC6 is a 59,374 square foot building at 21721 Filigree Court in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's 15-building cluster across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. The facility publishes N+1 redundancy for both UPS and generator systems and holds nine compliance certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and LEED certification. Equinix does not publish an IT load or power capacity figure in megawatts for DC6 itself, so the campus's role in AI scaling cannot be read from its own specifications.

Ashburn sits at the center of the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet, with roughly 10 million square feet of built capacity across all operators consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of power region-wide. Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Without DC6's published power capacity, it cannot be ranked against other AI-relevant facilities, though Virginia overall ranks 26th among US states by total published data center power capacity at 1,603.4 megawatts across 25 facilities with published figures out of 330 mapped sites in the state.

Starting January 1, 2027, Virginia's State Corporation Commission's new GS-5 rate class requires large data center customers like Equinix to sign 14-year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees under revised Dominion Energy rates. This regulatory lock-in makes multi-megawatt expansions at Ashburn a capital commitment over a fixed regulatory horizon, structuring how much new compute capacity this region can absorb during the remainder of the decade.
